analysis: What changed vs the 4:00 AM brief: the tape got worse, not better — S&P futures slid from -0.36% to -0.69% and Nasdaq futures from -0.97% to -1.46% by ~7:30 AM ET, and NVDA deepened from -1.6-2.2% to -3.84% premarket (~$156.59). Two new Nvidia threads landed: the WSJ reports the Trump administration plans to designate Nvidia and 20+ AI firms as US 'national champions' (single-source, unverified), and the 'Stand with Jensen' petition passed 171,000 signatures including ~8,500 current employees, while Polymarket puts a Huang return by year-end at just 16% — the campaign is loud, the market's odds are low. Bessent's 10-day deadline for export-control answers adds a Washington clock. The chip rout is now a premarket rout too: Micron -6.13%, CoreWeave -8.09%, AMD/Broadcom/Intel -3.5-5%. The one fresh company story is Amazon: a ULA Vulcan failure destroyed 40 Leo satellites Sunday, delaying its Starlink rival. MSFT faded from +0.88% to +0.05% premarket as the chip drag spread; AAPL (+0.47%) is the only megacap holding green. Bitcoin is holding above $64,000 but crypto-linked names (MSTR -8%) are not. Signal vs noise: the deepening futures slide, the chip-complex weakness, and the 10-year above 5% are real; the 'national champions' report and the petition are sentiment inputs, not decisions — the board and its Wachtell inquiry still hold the pen, and Tuesday's earnings remain the first hard data point.

headlines.headline: Futures deepen their slide into the open: at ~7:30 AM ET, S&P 500 futures -0.69%, Nasdaq 100 futures -1.46%, Dow futures -0.10% (Swingfolio). At 7:07 AM ET (CNBC): Nasdaq 100 futures -1.27%, S&P 500 -0.56%, Dow -0.04%. Friday closed split: S&P 500 7,561.67 (-0.40%), Nasdaq 25,136.27 (-0.91%), Dow 52,347.55 (+0.10%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The overnight fade accelerated since the 4:00 AM brief (S&P -0.36%, Nasdaq -0.97% then) — the open starts deeper in the red with tech leading down.

headlines.headline: Nvidia's slide deepens premarket: NVDA -3.84% to $156.59 at 7:32 AM ET (Swingfolio), -3.55% to $157.07 at 7:18 AM ET (CNBC), after falling ~13% last week to $162.85. The 'Stand with Jensen' petition passed 171,000 signatures by Monday morning, including ~8,500 current Nvidia employees and 90,000+ shareholders, backed by Elon Musk, Tim Sweeney, Garry Tan and Travis Kalanick; investors Gerstner and Baker urged the board to keep a return on the table. Polymarket puts a Huang return by Dec 31 at 16% (down from ~21%). Bessent gave the board 10 days to answer export-control compliance questions. Earnings are Tue Nov 17 after the close (consensus ~$108.9B revenue, ~$2.47 EPS; options imply a ~7% move).
headlines.why_it_matters: The comeback campaign is growing louder but the market's odds of a return are falling — and the stock keeps sliding into earnings, so the governance overhang is still the tape's main weight.

headlines.headline: The Trump administration plans to designate Nvidia and more than two dozen other AI companies as US 'national champions,' the WSJ reported Monday, citing people familiar with the plans. The report could not be independently verified.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source (WSJ, unnamed people) and unverified — if real, it would be a policy tailwind for Nvidia, but it is not a decision yet, so treat it as sentiment, not a catalyst.

headlines.headline: Chip complex routs premarket: Micron -6.13%, CoreWeave -8.09%, TSMC ADRs -5.30%, and Intel, AMD and Broadcom down 3.5-5% (Reuters/CNBC via Swingfolio). Asia set the tone overnight: Taiwan's Taiex -6.03%, TSMC -5.74% in Taipei, SK Hynix -5.5%, Samsung -3.2%, Nikkei -2.42%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The selloff is no longer just an Nvidia story — the whole AI hardware chain is repricing ahead of Tuesday's print, which drags the Nasdaq with it.

headlines.headline: Amazon's Leo satellite plan hit a setback: a ULA Vulcan rocket failed Sunday after liftoff from Cape Canaveral, destroying 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites. Amazon has contracted ULA for 38 Vulcan launches to deploy its planned 3,236-satellite network to rival Starlink. AMZN is -0.49% premarket to $265.35.
headlines.why_it_matters: A real schedule setback for Amazon's broadband buildout — the loss is small against Amazon's scale, but it delays a strategic program and adds to the premarket drag.

headlines.headline: Megacaps split premarket (Finnhub, ~7:50 AM ET): AAPL +0.47% to $357.95 after Friday's new 52-week high of $360.83; MSFT +0.05% to $524.16, fading from +0.88% earlier as the outage resolution and Stifel upgrade tailwind cools; META -0.78% to $636.69 after Friday's +2.90% close; AMZN -0.49%; TSLA -1.3% to $385.17. Baidu's US shares are down ~1% after Q3 revenue of 30.81B yuan ($4.62B) came in essentially in line with consensus, though EPS of $1.01 beat. Bitcoin is holding above $64,000 (~$64,300) but crypto-linked Strategy (MSTR) is off 8% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: Apple is the only megacap holding green — the rotation is narrowing to names without a fresh overhang, while Meta gives back part of Friday's gain and crypto-linked names stay under pressure.

headlines.headline: Fed focus today: Chair Kevin Warsh speaks at noon ET in San Francisco (AI and productivity), and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack also speaks Monday; FOMC minutes land Wednesday. Fed funds futures treat a December quarter-point hike as all but certain. Empire State manufacturing prints at 8:30 AM ET. The 2-year yield fell more than 2 bps Monday after its biggest weekly jump in over two years on Friday.
headlines.why_it_matters: With the hike fully priced, Warsh's tone is the day's rate signal — any hawkish surprise extends the pressure on growth multiples; a dovish lean would be the tape's easiest relief.
